newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Overnight guilder rates coast higher, seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Overnight guilder rates coast higher, seen easing.

text.p: Overnight guilder rates coasted higher on Tuesday but were seen easing on Wednesday when delayed social security payments flow into the market.
Call money traded most of the day between 3.00 and 3.25 percent, well above the 2.50 percent rate on special advances, although some traders reported deals at 2.93 percent.
"Short-term rates are up on the delay in social security payments," one dealer said. "They should return to more normal levels tomorrow."
He said overall trade had been dull, with little or no action in durations longer than one month.
Another dealer said early trade had been nervy, with many major players looking for call money.
This is unusual, as commercial banks tend to build up considerable savings towards the end of the customary three-month credit quota, which expires on Friday.
But call rates have been relatively high for some time now, prompting some dealers to speculate that at least one large bank has already used up its quota under the pact.
Tuesday's special advances allocation, a separate money market instrument used by the central bank to fine-tune liquidity, had been well-measured, dealers said.
"Overall the allocation is sufficient, there has just been a temporary tightness due to the brief delay in some payments," one said.
The guilder was quoting at around 112.20 guilders per 100 marks, unchanged from Monday's fixing.
